title: IBPS SO Prelims Mock Test - Verbal Ability - Mock 1

questions.direction: Read the passage carefully and answer the question.
questions.passage: The rapid expansion of digital payments has transformed the way consumers and businesses conduct transactions. While digital platforms offer convenience and speed, their growing use has also increased concerns regarding cybersecurity and data privacy. Experts argue that technological advancement alone cannot guarantee secure transactions. Users must also adopt responsible practices, such as using strong passwords, enabling two-factor authentication and avoiding suspicious links. Financial institutions, meanwhile, need to strengthen their security infrastructure and educate customers about emerging threats.
questions.text: Which of the following can be most appropriately inferred from the passage?
options: Digital payments are likely to completely replace cash transactions.
Cybersecurity can be ensured solely through advanced technology.
Both service providers and users have responsibilities in maintaining digital payment security.
Users should avoid digital payment platforms because they are inherently unsafe.
Financial institutions are primarily responsible for all cybersecurity failures.
questions.explanation: The passage states that users must adopt responsible practices while financial institutions must strengthen security and educate customers. Therefore, both users and service providers share responsibility.

questions.direction: Read the passage carefully and answer the question.
questions.passage: Urban transport systems are under increasing pressure as cities expand and private vehicle ownership rises. Merely widening roads may provide temporary relief but often encourages greater dependence on private vehicles. A sustainable solution requires investment in reliable public transportation, safe pedestrian infrastructure and efficient cycling networks. Such measures can reduce congestion while also lowering pollution and improving accessibility for people who cannot afford private vehicles.
questions.text: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT mentioned as a benefit of sustainable urban transport?
options: Reduction in dependence on private vehicles
questions.explanation: The passage mentions reducing congestion, lowering pollution, improving accessibility and reducing dependence on private vehicles. It does not mention an increase in private vehicle ownership as a benefit.

questions.direction: Read the passage carefully and answer the question.
questions.passage: Many organizations have adopted hybrid work models after observing that flexibility can improve employee satisfaction. However, flexibility does not automatically lead to higher productivity. Without clear communication, measurable goals and effective collaboration tools, employees may struggle to coordinate their work. Managers therefore need to focus less on physical presence and more on outcomes, while ensuring that employees have adequate support.
questions.text: What is the central idea of the passage?
options: Employees are always more productive when working from home.
Physical presence is essential for effective management.
Hybrid work can be beneficial, but its success depends on effective management and support.
Organizations should completely abandon office-based work.
Employee satisfaction has no relationship with workplace flexibility.
questions.explanation: The passage acknowledges the benefits of flexibility but emphasizes that hybrid work requires communication, measurable goals, collaboration tools and managerial support.

questions.direction: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
questions.text: The committee has decided (A)/ to postpone the meeting (B)/ because several members was unavailable (C)/ at the scheduled time. (D)/ No error (E)
questions.explanation: The subject 'several members' is plural, so 'was' should be replaced with 'were'.

questions.direction: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
questions.text: Neither the manager nor his assistants (A)/ was willing to take responsibility (B)/ for the delay caused by the technical issue. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject nearer to it. 'Assistants' is plural, so 'was' should be 'were'.

questions.direction: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
questions.text: The report, along with several supporting documents, (A)/ were submitted to the committee (B)/ before the deadline expired. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: The main subject is 'The report', which is singular. The phrase 'along with several supporting documents' does not change the subject. Therefore, 'were' should be 'was'.

questions.direction: Choose the word that best replaces the underlined phrase.
questions.text: The management decided to look into the matter before taking disciplinary action.
questions.explanation: 'Look into' means to investigate or examine something carefully.

questions.direction: Choose the word that is most similar in meaning to the given word.
questions.text: PRUDENT
questions.explanation: Prudent means acting with care and good judgment. 'Cautious' is the closest synonym.

questions.direction: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to the given word.
questions.text: RELUCTANT
questions.explanation: Reluctant means unwilling or hesitant. 'Eager' is its opposite.

questions.direction: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.
questions.text: The new policy was introduced to ______ transparency in the recruitment process.
questions.explanation: 'Enhance' means to improve or increase the quality or value of something. It fits the context of increasing transparency.

questions.direction: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.
questions.text: Despite several warnings, the employee continued to ______ the importance of following security protocols.
questions.explanation: The context indicates that the employee failed to recognize the importance. Therefore, 'underestimate' is the appropriate word.

questions.direction: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate word.
questions.text: The sudden decline in demand forced the company to ______ its expansion plans.
questions.explanation: 'Reconsider' means to think again about a decision or plan, which fits the context.

questions.direction: Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
questions.text:
A. As a result, many organizations are investing heavily in employee training.
B. Cybersecurity threats have become increasingly sophisticated in recent years.
C. Human error remains one of the most common causes of security breaches.
D. Technical safeguards alone, therefore, cannot completely eliminate the risk.
E. Employees need to understand how their everyday actions can expose an organization to threats.
questions.explanation: B introduces the issue, C identifies human error, A gives the resulting organizational response, D provides the conclusion about technical safeguards, and E explains what employees need to understand. Hence B-C-A-D-E.

questions.direction: Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
questions.text:
A. This has made it easier for small businesses to reach customers beyond their local markets.
B. E-commerce platforms have significantly changed the retail landscape.
C. However, increased competition has also forced sellers to improve pricing and customer service.
D. Consumers can now compare products from multiple sellers within minutes.
E. Consequently, businesses need to adapt continuously to remain competitive.
questions.explanation: B introduces e-commerce, D explains a consumer benefit, C introduces the resulting competition, A explains another consequence for small businesses, and E concludes with the need to adapt. Therefore B-D-C-A-E.

questions.direction: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.
questions.text: The proposal was initially rejected because the committee found it financially ______ and operationally difficult to implement.
questions.explanation: The sentence indicates that the proposal was rejected because it was financially unsuitable. 'Unreasonable' best fits the negative context.

questions.direction: Read the passage carefully and answer the question.
questions.passage: Artificial intelligence is increasingly being used to automate repetitive tasks across industries. This does not necessarily mean that human workers will become irrelevant. In many cases, automation changes the nature of work by reducing routine responsibilities and allowing employees to focus on judgment, creativity and interpersonal tasks. However, workers may need to acquire new skills to adapt to these changing requirements.
questions.text: Which of the following is most strongly supported by the passage?
options: AI will eliminate all forms of human employment.
Automation can change job responsibilities without necessarily eliminating human workers.
Creative work will eventually be performed entirely by AI.
Workers do not need to acquire new skills because AI handles routine tasks.
AI adoption is limited to the technology industry.
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly states that automation can reduce routine responsibilities while allowing humans to focus on judgment, creativity and interpersonal work.

questions.direction: Read the passage carefully and answer the question.
questions.passage: Financial literacy enables individuals to make informed decisions about saving, borrowing and investing. Yet access to financial information alone is not sufficient. Individuals must also understand how to evaluate risks, compare alternatives and plan according to their financial circumstances. Schools and financial institutions can play an important role by providing practical education rather than merely presenting theoretical concepts.
questions.text: Which of the following can be inferred from the passage?
options: Financial information is unnecessary for making financial decisions.
Financial literacy should focus only on investment strategies.
Practical financial education may be more useful than information without guidance on its application.
Schools should stop teaching financial concepts.
Financial institutions should make investment decisions on behalf of individuals.
questions.explanation: The passage contrasts access to information with the ability to evaluate risks and apply knowledge practically. Therefore, practical financial education is emphasized.

questions.direction: Choose the most appropriate phrase to complete the sentence.
questions.text: The CEO's decision to step down came as a surprise, ______ several analysts had predicted leadership changes earlier.
questions.explanation: The sentence contrasts the surprise with the fact that analysts had predicted leadership changes. 'Although' correctly expresses this contrast.

questions.direction: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
questions.text: Select the correct sentence.
options: Each of the employees have submitted their report.
Each of the employees has submitted his or her report.
Each of the employees have submitted his report.
Each employees has submitted their reports.
Each of employees have submitted his or her report.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular and therefore takes the singular verb 'has'. The correct sentence is 'Each of the employees has submitted his or her report.'

questions.direction: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
questions.text: Select the correct sentence.
options: No sooner the meeting had started than the lights went out.
No sooner had the meeting started when the lights went out.
No sooner had the meeting started than the lights went out.
No sooner did the meeting started than the lights went out.
No sooner had the meeting start than the lights went out.
questions.explanation: The correct construction is 'No sooner had + subject + past participle + than'. Therefore, option C is correct.

questions.direction: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.
questions.text: The report was criticized for being ______, as it presented several claims without sufficient evidence.
questions.explanation: 'Unsubstantiated' means not supported by evidence, which directly matches the context.

questions.direction: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank.
questions.text: The management's decision to ______ the outdated software was welcomed by employees who had struggled with frequent system failures.
questions.explanation: Since the software is outdated and causes failures, management would replace it. Therefore, 'replace' is correct.

questions.direction: Read the passage carefully and answer the question.
questions.passage: Remote banking has expanded access to financial services, particularly for customers living far from physical branches. Nevertheless, digital exclusion remains a concern. Elderly customers, people with limited digital skills and those living in areas with poor internet connectivity may find online services difficult to use. Banks therefore need to combine digital innovation with accessible alternatives and customer support.
questions.text: What is the primary concern highlighted in the passage?
options: Banks are closing branches too slowly.
Digital banking is reducing the number of financial services available.
Some groups may be unable to benefit fully from digital banking because of digital or infrastructural limitations.
Customers prefer physical branches over online services.
Internet connectivity has improved equally across all regions.
questions.explanation: The passage highlights digital exclusion among elderly customers, people with limited digital skills and people in areas with poor connectivity.

questions.direction: Identify the part of the sentence that contains an error.
questions.text: Having completed the project ahead of schedule, (A)/ the team was praised by the manager (B)/ for their efficiency and commitment. (C)/ No error (D)
questions.explanation: In traditional formal grammar, the singular noun 'team' should be referred to consistently. 'For its efficiency and commitment' is preferred.

questions.direction: Choose the word that is most similar in meaning to the given word.
questions.text: MITIGATE
questions.explanation: Mitigate means to make something less severe, serious or painful. 'Alleviate' is the closest synonym.
